chapter_summary: Proverbs 19 lays out a wide canvas of wisdom: the superiority of integrity over wealth, the danger of lies and lazy living, the blessing of a wise family life, and the life-giving power of fearing the LORD. Solomon contrasts the fool — who blames God for his own bad choices — with the wise person who hears correction and grows. Obedience and discipline are presented as acts of love, not cruelty. At the centre of the chapter is a profound truth: God's plans always stand, no matter what people scheme.
main_lesson: Being honest and doing right is better than having lots of things. God's plans always win, and He rewards those who respect Him.

memory_verse.kjv: There are many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.
memory_verse.little_bible: People make many plans. But only God's plans always stand.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 19 is an ideal chapter for discussing integrity under pressure — particularly the pressure that wealth, popularity, and anger create. Verse 1 opens with a bold claim: a poor person who walks in integrity is better than a wealthy fool. This is countercultural and children need to hear it clearly and often. The chapter also gives parents a natural opening to discuss why lying is always dangerous (verses 5 and 9), why laziness destroys (verse 15), and why discipline is love (verse 18).

Verse 21 — the memory verse — is one of the most comforting in all of Proverbs: no matter what plans people make, God's counsel is the one that prevails. For anxious children, this is deeply reassuring. For children who feel powerless in a world of adult decisions, it reminds them that the God who loves them is in charge of all outcomes.

Verse 17 is extraordinary and deserves special attention: lending to the poor is treated as lending to God, who will repay. This is a stunning elevation of generosity. Finally, verse 23 ties together the whole chapter: the fear of the LORD leads to life, satisfaction, and safety. Holiness is not a burden — it is the path to the life God designed for us.

Encourage your family to practise verse 17 this week: find one practical way to give to or help someone who cannot repay you.
application_for_children: This week, choose honesty over excuses, even if it is hard. Remember that God sees everything and His plans always win. Help someone who cannot pay you back.

verses.kjv: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, than he that is perverse in his lips, and is a fool.
verses.little_bible: It is better to be poor and honest. Being rich but dishonest makes you a fool.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Being honest is better than being rich and dishonest.
verses.meaning: Solomon makes a striking comparison: a poor person with integrity — consistent, truthful character — is worth more than a wealthy person whose speech is twisted and whose life is foolish. Wealth without wisdom is a liability. Character without wealth is still honourable. This proverb challenges every cultural instinct that prizes wealth above integrity.
verses.prayer: God, help me choose honesty over everything else.
verses.discussion_question: Why is being honest better than being rich?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children resist the cultural message that wealth and popularity are the highest goals — and instead build a deep love for integrity even when it costs them?
verses.do_it_today: Choose to tell the truth today, even if it is hard or costs you something.
verses.illustration_prompt: A smiling child in simple clothes walking a straight bright path, and a richly dressed figure stumbling on a crooked road, soft watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Also, that the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.
verses.little_bible: Acting without knowing is not good. Rushing ahead without thinking leads to doing wrong.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Think before you act. Rushing causes mistakes.
verses.meaning: Zeal without knowledge is dangerous. Acting quickly without understanding the situation — or God's wisdom — produces sin. Solomon pairs ignorance with haste: both lead to the same outcome. True wisdom requires pausing to gather knowledge before acting. Impulsiveness, even with good intentions, can cause harm.
verses.prayer: God, help me think before I rush into things.
verses.discussion_question: What can go wrong when you act too fast?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children slow down and seek wisdom before making decisions — building the habit of pausing, praying, and thinking before acting?
verses.do_it_today: Before your next decision today, pause and think: do I know enough? Is this right?
verses.illustration_prompt: A child running ahead of a path that curves into darkness, while a wise child pauses and looks at a lit signpost, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The foolishness of man perverteth his way: and his heart fretteth against the LORD.
verses.little_bible: When people make foolish choices, their life goes wrong. Then they blame God instead of themselves.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Bad choices ruin your path. Don't blame God for them.
verses.meaning: One of Scripture's most searching observations: when a person's foolish decisions destroy their life, they turn around and are angry at God. Their own choices have perverted their way, but their heart blames the LORD. This is the anatomy of pride — refusing to own our own wrongdoing and projecting blame upward. Repentance begins by seeing our own part clearly.
verses.prayer: God, help me never blame You for my own wrong choices.
verses.discussion_question: Who is really to blame when bad choices go wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children take responsibility for their own choices rather than externalising blame — and how do we model that ourselves as parents?
verses.do_it_today: If something went wrong recently, ask honestly: did my own choice cause this? Take responsibility before God today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child looking at a tangled mess of their own making, then pointing upward in blame, while a wise child quietly bows and says sorry, warm watercolour

verses.kjv: Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.
verses.little_bible: Rich people attract many friends. But a poor person is often left alone.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wealth brings many friends. Poverty can leave you alone.
verses.meaning: Solomon is making an observation about human nature, not a command. Wealth attracts people who want something; poverty drives them away. This is the world's way — using people for what they have rather than loving them for who they are. The proverb implicitly calls readers to be different: to value people regardless of their wealth.
verses.prayer: God, help me love people for who they are, not what they have.
verses.discussion_question: Should we choose friends because they are rich?
verses.family_discussion: How do we instil in our children a love for people that is not based on what those people can offer them — and how do we help them reach out to those who are lonely or poor?
verses.do_it_today: Be friendly today to someone who might feel left out or overlooked.
verses.illustration_prompt: A crowd gathered around a figure with gold coins, while a poor child stands apart and one kind child walks over to befriend them, soft watercolour

verses.kjv: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall not escape.
verses.little_bible: A person who lies will be punished. No one who speaks lies will escape.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Liars will not escape punishment. God sees every lie.
verses.meaning: God holds lying witnesses to a strict account. This proverb speaks directly into courtroom settings — false testimony is a grave sin — but it extends to all dishonest speech. There is no hiding from God's knowledge or from the consequences that come with deceit. The certainty of punishment is a mercy: it makes the world just.
verses.prayer: God, help me always tell the truth.
verses.discussion_question: Why does God take lying so seriously?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that dishonesty is not a minor flaw but a serious sin with real consequences — and that God's justice is not negotiable?
verses.do_it_today: If you said something untrue recently, go back and correct it honestly today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure speaking false words that form visible chains binding their own feet, while the truth shines as a bright light above them, warm watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Many will intreat the favour of the prince: and every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts.
verses.little_bible: Everyone wants to please a powerful person. And everyone wants to be friends with someone who gives gifts.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People try to get close to those who are powerful or give gifts.
verses.meaning: Solomon observes that self-interest drives human relationships with the powerful. People seek the favour of rulers and attach themselves to generous givers — not out of genuine love but out of what they hope to gain. This is an astute observation about flattery and false friendship, preparing the reader to value authentic relationship over calculated connection.
verses.prayer: God, help me be a true friend, not a selfish one.
verses.discussion_question: What makes a friendship truly real?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children recognise the difference between people who genuinely love them and those who are only around for what they can get — and how do we model and build authentic relationships?
verses.do_it_today: Do something kind for a friend today with no expectation of anything back.
verses.illustration_prompt: A crowd eagerly gathering around a prince and a gift-giver, while one quiet child gives a gift to a friend with nothing to gain, gentle watercolour

verses.kjv: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth them with words, yet they are wanting to him.
verses.little_bible: When someone is poor, even family can turn away. Friends leave too. The poor person calls after them, but no one comes back.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Even family can leave a poor person. It is very sad and unfair.
verses.meaning: The isolation of poverty is one of life's harshest realities: even family members withdraw from those in need, and friends disappear when there is nothing to gain. The poor person's appeals go unanswered. Solomon is not endorsing this behaviour — he is exposing it as the painful opposite of how God calls us to treat the vulnerable.
verses.prayer: God, help me stand by those who are poor and alone.
verses.discussion_question: How should we treat people who are going through hard times?
verses.family_discussion: How do we build in our household a culture of loyal love that does not walk away when people can no longer benefit us — a love that mirrors God's faithful love?
verses.do_it_today: Think of someone going through a hard time. Send them a message or do something to show you are still there for them.
verses.illustration_prompt: A lonely child stretching out a hand as others walk away, and one faithful friend turning back to hold that hand, warm compassionate watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: he that keepeth understanding shall find good.
verses.little_bible: Getting wisdom is loving yourself well. Holding on to wisdom leads to good things.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wisdom is good for your whole life. Hold on to it.
verses.meaning: Pursuing wisdom is not selfish — it is self-care in the deepest sense. The person who loves their own soul will seek wisdom, because wisdom protects, guides, and sustains the soul. Keeping understanding means not letting it go — holding to what God teaches even when the world pulls another way. The reward is simply described: finding good.
verses.prayer: God, help me love wisdom and hold on to it.
verses.discussion_question: How does getting wisdom help your whole life?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that seeking wisdom and knowledge of God is the best investment they can make in themselves — better than any skill, talent, or possession?
verses.do_it_today: Read or learn something wise today and ask God to help it stick with you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child holding a glowing book of wisdom close to their heart, light radiating outward in warm golden tones, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall perish.
verses.little_bible: A lying witness will be punished. A person who keeps speaking lies will be destroyed.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Lying always has serious consequences. It leads to destruction.
verses.meaning: A direct repetition and intensification of verse 5: the consequence here is not just punishment but perishing — a word that implies total ruin. The doubling within the same chapter underscores how seriously God views dishonest testimony. Persistent, unrepentant lying ends in destruction. Truthfulness is not optional; it is a matter of life and death.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from lies that destroy my life.
verses.discussion_question: What is the final result of a life full of lying?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that dishonesty, left unchecked, compounds — each lie requiring more lies, until the whole structure collapses? How does this connect to the freedom of truth?
verses.do_it_today: Ask God to help you tell the truth even when it is difficult or embarrassing.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure tangled in growing webs of false words that slowly collapse around them, while the truth stands as a solid unshaken pillar, stark watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: Delight is not seemly for a fool; much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
verses.little_bible: A fool enjoying luxury does not fit. It is even worse when a servant rules over princes.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some things do not fit. A fool should not live in luxury.
verses.meaning: Solomon speaks to the disorder that arises when wisdom and position are mismatched. A fool in comfort is dangerous because comfort without wisdom produces pride and foolishness without restraint. A servant ruling over princes represents a chaotic inversion of proper order. The proverb calls for character to precede position.
verses.prayer: God, give me the wisdom to match any position I hold.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to grow wise before gaining power?
verses.family_discussion: How do we prepare our children for leadership and responsibility — teaching them that character must always precede authority, and that influence without wisdom is dangerous?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one area where you have been given responsibility. Ask God for the wisdom to handle it well.
verses.illustration_prompt: A fool seated on a throne with a crown sitting crooked, surrounded by confusion, while a wise young person studies quietly in the corner, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
verses.little_bible: A wise person is slow to get angry. It is something to be proud of when you forgive someone who did wrong.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Being slow to get angry is wise. Forgiving others is something to be proud of.
verses.meaning: Self-control in the face of provocation is a mark of wisdom. The wise person delays anger — giving time for understanding, perspective, and mercy to intervene. But even more: overlooking an offence is presented as glory, not weakness. True dignity does not demand every wrong be avenged. This anticipates the New Testament pattern of forgiveness.
verses.prayer: God, make me slow to anger and quick to forgive.
verses.discussion_question: Why is forgiving someone something to be proud of?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate slow anger and ready forgiveness in our households — not as passivity or doormat behaviour, but as the confident, God-reflecting response of someone secure in their identity?
verses.do_it_today: If someone has upset you recently, choose today to forgive them — even privately before God.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child breathing deeply and letting go of a balloon labelled 'anger,' their face peaceful, another child looking relieved nearby, soft watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The king's wrath is as the roaring of a lion; but his favour is as dew upon the grass.
verses.little_bible: A king's anger is terrifying, like a roaring lion. But his kindness is refreshing, like dew on the grass.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A king's anger is frightening. His kindness is like cool morning dew.
verses.meaning: The contrasting images — a roaring lion and dew upon grass — describe the enormous range of a ruler's power to harm or to refresh. Kings have extraordinary capacity for both terror and blessing. The proverb implicitly calls those in authority to be sources of refreshment, not destruction. It also prepares the mind for thinking about God as the ultimate King whose favour gives life.
verses.prayer: God, let my kindness refresh the people around me.
verses.discussion_question: What does it feel like when someone in charge is kind to you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we as parents and leaders use our authority to refresh and bless those under our care rather than to frighten or control them? How does this reflect God's character?
verses.do_it_today: Use your words today to refresh someone. Say something encouraging to a person who needs it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A lion roaring on one side, and on the other side soft morning dew on a bright green field, a child choosing to walk toward the gentle side, warm watercolour

verses.kjv: A foolish son is the calamity of his father: and the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.
verses.little_bible: A foolish child brings disaster to their father. A quarrelsome person in the home is like a leaking roof that never stops.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A foolish child hurts their family. Constant arguing ruins a home.
verses.meaning: Solomon speaks to two household trials that wear a person down. A foolish son is a calamity — not an inconvenience but a disaster that follows the father. Contentious arguing in the home is compared to a dripping roof: not one sudden flood but the relentless, exhausting drip that makes a house unliveable. Harmony in the home is a gift to everyone who lives there.
verses.prayer: God, help me bring peace, not arguing, into my home.
verses.discussion_question: How does constant arguing make a home feel?
verses.family_discussion: How do we build a household culture where disagreements are handled without contempt or repeated contention — and how do we model godly conflict resolution for our children?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one way to bring peace into your home today — stop an argument, say sorry, or do something kind without being asked.
verses.illustration_prompt: A house with a dripping roof under a grey cloud on one side, and a bright house full of warmth and peace on the other, a child choosing to walk into the peaceful home, watercolour

verses.kjv: House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from the LORD.
verses.little_bible: A family can pass down a house and money. But a wise and good partner is a gift from God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Parents can give us things. But a wise, good partner is a gift from God.
verses.meaning: Material inheritance — house and riches — can be passed from father to child through human effort and planning. But a wise and discerning spouse is in a different category altogether: it is a gift from the LORD. No amount of human effort or matchmaking produces this; it is a grace. This proverb elevates marriage far above a transaction and places it firmly in the realm of divine providence.
verses.memory_phrase: A good partner is God's gift.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for the good gifts You give to families.
verses.discussion_question: Why is a wise and good person in your family a gift from God?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to see a faithful, wise spouse as something to pray for, wait for, and be prepared for — not something to rush into or treat as an entitlement?
verses.do_it_today: Thank God today for the people He has placed in your family. Ask Him to make you a wise and kind person for others.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two parents and a child in a warm home, a gentle golden light coming through the window as if from God, the family holding hands, soft watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; and an idle soul shall suffer hunger.
verses.little_bible: Being lazy sends you into a deep sleep. A person who does nothing will go hungry.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Laziness makes you sleep your life away. Then you go hungry.
verses.meaning: Sloth — deep, habitual laziness — is presented as a kind of stupor: it casts a person into heavy sleep, disconnecting them from the responsibilities of life. The consequence is not symbolic but literal: the idle soul suffers hunger. Laziness is not harmless; it has real material consequences. Work is a gift and a calling, not a curse.
verses.prayer: God, help me work hard and not be lazy.
verses.discussion_question: What happens to someone who is always too lazy to work?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate diligence in our children — not by pressure and anxiety, but by helping them see work as purposeful, God-honouring, and connected to real outcomes in life?
verses.do_it_today: Do one task today that you have been avoiding. Do it fully and well.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sleeping heavily while their responsibilities pile up around them, then looking hungry and regretful, contrasted with a child working cheerfully, watercolour

verses.kjv: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; but he that despiseth his ways shall die.
verses.little_bible: Obeying God's commands protects your own life. Refusing to obey God leads to death.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Obeying God keeps you safe. Ignoring God's ways is dangerous.
verses.meaning: Obedience to God's commandments is life-preserving: keeping God's word is the same as keeping one's own soul. This is not merely external law-keeping but a profound connection between obedience and life itself. To despise God's ways — to treat them with contempt — leads to death. The stakes of obedience and disobedience could not be higher.
verses.prayer: God, help me obey You and protect my life.
verses.discussion_question: How does obeying God protect your life?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that God's commands are not restrictions that take away freedom but guardrails that protect and give life — and that disobedience has real, serious consequences?
verses.do_it_today: Choose to obey one of God's commands today that you find difficult. Ask God for strength to do it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child on a safe bright path following clear signposts, and another figure straying off into darkness, the contrast shown in warm and cool tones, watercolour

verses.kjv: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
verses.little_bible: When you help someone poor, you are lending to God. And God will pay you back.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Helping poor people is like lending to God. He will repay you.
verses.meaning: This verse contains one of the most astonishing promises in Proverbs: generosity to the poor is treated as a loan to God Himself. God takes it personally and personally repays it. This elevates every act of compassion into a transaction with the Almighty. No act of genuine generosity toward the vulnerable is ever lost — God keeps the books and He pays.
verses.prayer: God, help me give to the poor and trust You to repay.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to lend to God by helping a poor person?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate radical generosity toward the poor in our family — not reluctant giving but joyful, trusting giving that believes God's promise to repay? What opportunities can we find together?
verses.do_it_today: Find one way today to help someone who has less than you — give money, food, time, or a kind word.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child handing bread to a poor child, and a gentle divine light descending as if in receipt, written words 'I will repay' in soft golden lettering, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.
verses.little_bible: Correct your child while there is still time to help them. Do not hold back correction just because they cry.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Parents should correct their children while there is still hope. It is an act of love.
verses.meaning: Discipline is urgent and time-sensitive: there is a window of hope in which correction shapes a child's character. Missing that window is a parental failure. The instruction not to spare for crying means that a child's emotional protest should not stop necessary correction — love sometimes means persisting through discomfort for the child's long-term good. This is not cruelty; it is urgent love.
verses.memory_phrase: Correct now, while there is hope.
verses.prayer: God, help parents love their children with wise correction.
verses.discussion_question: Why is correcting a child early an act of love?
verses.family_discussion: How do we balance firmness and tenderness in discipline — being neither so soft that we fail our children nor so harsh that we wound them? How do we communicate love even in correction?
verses.do_it_today: Parents: if there is a correction you have been putting off, address it today with love, firmness, and prayer.
verses.illustration_prompt: A parent gently but firmly holding a child who is upset, their face showing love, not anger, warm sunset light through a window, soft watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: for if thou deliver him, yet thou must do it again.
verses.little_bible: A very angry person will keep getting into trouble. If you rescue them, you will have to rescue them again.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: An angry person who is always rescued never changes. They keep getting into trouble.
verses.meaning: Chronic anger produces recurring consequences. The warning here is also directed at helpers: rescuing a wrathful person from consequences without addressing the root anger does not help them — it enables them. Real help addresses the heart, not just the situation. Repeated rescuing of an unchanged person is futile, even harmful to them.
verses.prayer: God, help me deal with anger before it deals with me.
verses.discussion_question: Why does rescuing an angry person over and over not really help them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see that managing anger at its root is more important than being rescued from its consequences — and how do we model healthy emotional regulation ourselves?
verses.do_it_today: If anger is a pattern in your life, ask God today to help you deal with it at the root, not just the surface.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure in repeated cycles of anger and trouble being picked up again and again, while a wise person beside them gently points to the heart as the source, watercolour

verses.kjv: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
verses.little_bible: Listen to good advice. Receive teaching. This will make you wise as you grow older.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Listen to advice and teaching. It will make you wise one day.
verses.meaning: Wisdom is cumulative: the person who builds a lifetime habit of listening to counsel and receiving instruction arrives at old age with wisdom as their companion. The phrase 'latter end' is future-oriented — wisdom is an investment made now for a harvest later. No one becomes wise accidentally; it is the fruit of a sustained willingness to hear and receive.
verses.prayer: God, help me listen to good advice and grow wise.
verses.discussion_question: How does listening to good advice help you in the future?
verses.family_discussion: How do we build in our children a love of receiving counsel — helping them see correction and instruction not as insults to their intelligence but as investments in their future?
verses.do_it_today: Ask a wise person in your life for one piece of advice. Really listen and write it down.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting attentively with an elder who is sharing wisdom, a small tree growing between them to represent future growth, warm golden watercolour scene

verses.kjv: There are many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.
verses.little_bible: People make many plans. But only God's plans always stand and come true.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: You can make lots of plans. But only God's plans always come true.
verses.meaning: Human planning is vast and creative, but it is subject to failure, change, and divine overrule. God's counsel — His purposes, plans, and decrees — is the only thing that is guaranteed to stand. This is not fatalism but reassurance: the universe is not at the mercy of human schemes. God's word will accomplish what He intends. Our best response is to align our plans with His.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust Your plans more than my own.
verses.discussion_question: Why is God's plan the only one that always comes true?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children hold their plans loosely and trust God's plans deeply — teaching them to pray 'Your will be done' and mean it, even when God's plan differs from their own?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one plan you have. Then pray and offer it to God: 'Lord, your plan is better. I trust You.'
verses.illustration_prompt: Many arrows and plans scattered around a figure while one straight golden path from above stands firm through all of them, a child looking up in trust, watercolour

verses.kjv: The desire of a man is his kindness: and a poor man is better than a liar.
verses.little_bible: What makes a person truly desirable is their kindness. A poor person who is honest is worth more than a rich liar.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Kindness makes a person truly worth knowing. Honesty matters more than riches.
verses.meaning: True attractiveness — what makes a person genuinely desirable as a companion and friend — is their kindness, not their wealth or status. And again the poor-vs-liar contrast: poverty is not shameful, but lying is. A poor honest person has more worth than a wealthy deceiver. Character is the true measure of a person.
verses.prayer: God, make me kind and honest above all else.
verses.discussion_question: What makes a person truly worth knowing?
verses.family_discussion: How do we communicate to our children that their value is not in their achievements, possessions, or appearance but in the kindness and honesty of their character — and how do we reinforce that consistently?
verses.do_it_today: Do one act of genuine kindness today, with no audience and no recognition expected.
verses.illustration_prompt: A poorly dressed child glowing with warm light as they share what little they have, while a richly dressed figure in shadow holds back in dishonesty, soft watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: The fear of the LORD tendeth to life: and he that hath it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.
verses.little_bible: Respecting God and honouring Him leads to life. Those who do will be satisfied. Evil will not overtake them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honouring God leads to life. God keeps those who respect Him safe.
verses.meaning: The fear of the LORD — reverential awe, holy respect for God's greatness and authority — is the path to life in all its fullness. The one who has this holy reverence lives in satisfaction and is kept from the worst evils. This is not a health-and-wealth promise but a description of the flourishing that comes from being rightly aligned with God. Holiness is not a burden; it is a life-giving orientation.
verses.prayer: God, help me always respect and honour You.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to respect and honour God with your life?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a holy reverence for God in our children — not terror, but deep awe and love that shapes how they think, speak, and live? What does this look like in daily family life?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one way you can show more respect and honour to God in your daily routine. Do it today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing in gentle awe before a beautiful sunrise, arms slightly raised in reverence, a bright path ahead lit by God's presence, warm glowing watercolour

verses.kjv: A slothful man hideth his hand in his bosom, and will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.
verses.little_bible: A lazy person tucks their hand away and will not even lift food to eat. Their laziness is extreme.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A very lazy person will not even lift their hand to eat. Laziness can go very far.
verses.meaning: This proverb uses vivid, almost comical exaggeration to expose the absurdity of extreme laziness. A man so slothful he will not even raise his hand to eat is a picture of someone who has let laziness consume them entirely. It is meant to shock the reader into self-examination: are there areas of our lives where we have become that unwilling to make even basic effort?
verses.prayer: God, help me not be too lazy to do what I must do.
verses.discussion_question: What is wrong with being so lazy you will not even help yourself?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see laziness as a spiritual problem — not just a personality type — that robs them of potential, relationships, and purpose? What habits build diligence?
verses.do_it_today: Pick one thing you have been too lazy to do and do it today, even if it is small.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting with food beside them, hand tucked in, looking sleepy and stubborn, while another child works cheerfully nearby with a bright smile, playful watercolour

verses.kjv: Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware: and reprove one that hath understanding, and he will understand knowledge.
verses.little_bible: Punish a mocker and a simple person will learn to be careful. Correct a wise person and they will understand even more.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A punishment can teach others to be careful. A wise person learns more from correction.
verses.meaning: Different people respond to correction differently. A scorner — one who mocks wisdom — may not personally learn from punishment, but watching consequences fall on mockers makes simple, impressionable people more cautious. But a person of understanding needs only a reproof: they take correction and gain knowledge. Wisdom recognises what kind of person it is dealing with and responds accordingly.
verses.prayer: God, help me be someone who learns from correction.
verses.discussion_question: Why do wise people grow more when they are corrected?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children become people who receive correction as a gift rather than an attack — cultivating the humility that allows them to learn from every reproof they receive?
verses.do_it_today: When someone corrects you today, pause before reacting. Ask: what can I learn from this?
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise child listening attentively as a teacher corrects them, growing visibly taller and brighter from the instruction, warm encouraging watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that wasteth his father, and chaseth away his mother, is a son that causeth shame, and bringeth reproach.
verses.little_bible: A child who dishonours their father and drives away their mother brings great shame on the family.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Treating parents badly brings great shame. Honour your parents.
verses.meaning: Mistreating parents — wasting a father's resources, driving away a mother — is not merely a family problem; it is a public shame. The Hebrew words for 'wasteth' and 'chaseth away' imply violence and force. This proverb reinforces the fifth commandment: honouring parents is serious before God and before society. The consequences of dishonour are both relational and reputational.
verses.prayer: God, help me honour my parents every day.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it so important to treat your parents with respect?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that honouring parents is not just about behaviour in the moment but about a lifelong posture of gratitude, love, and respect for those God placed over them?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today to honour your parents — say thank you, help without being asked, or write them a kind note.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child holding open a door for their parent with a warm respectful smile, sunlight filling the scene, a family home glowing with love, soft watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Cease, my son, to hear the instruction that causeth to err from the words of knowledge.
verses.little_bible: My son, stop listening to teaching that leads you away from God's truth. Not all teaching is good.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Stop listening to anything that leads you away from God's truth.
verses.meaning: A startling verse: Solomon tells his son to stop listening — but specifically to stop listening to instruction that leads away from knowledge. Not all teaching is trustworthy. The child must develop discernment: able to recognise voices that sound wise but lead away from God's word. This is a call to guard what enters the ear and the heart.
verses.prayer: God, help me only listen to what leads me closer to You.
verses.discussion_question: How can you tell if teaching is leading you toward or away from God?
verses.family_discussion: How do we equip our children with the discernment to evaluate what they hear — from peers, media, teachers, and culture — measuring it against God's word rather than accepting it uncritically?
verses.do_it_today: Think about one voice in your life — a show, a song, a friend — that might be leading you away from God's truth. Pray about it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child at a fork in a road, one path glowing with God's word, the other leading into fog, a wise elder pointing gently toward the lit path, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: An ungodly witness scorneth judgment: and the mouth of the wicked devoureth iniquity.
verses.little_bible: A wicked witness mocks justice. The wicked person eats up wrongdoing like it is food.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A wicked witness hates justice. Wicked people love doing wrong.
verses.meaning: Two devastating portraits: the ungodly witness scorns the very judgment that exists to establish truth — they mock justice itself. And the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity, meaning sin is not something they stumble into but something they consume eagerly. Wickedness at this level has become an appetite. This proverb exposes the darkness that lies beneath a life that rejects God's standards.
verses.prayer: God, keep my heart from loving what is wrong.
verses.discussion_question: What is dangerous about someone who enjoys doing wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that sin is not merely a bad habit but, left unchecked, becomes an appetite — a love for wrong? How does the Gospel address even this deep-level corruption?
verses.do_it_today: Ask God to search your heart today: is there anything wrong that you have started to enjoy or excuse? Bring it to Him honestly.
verses.illustration_prompt: A shadowed figure greedily consuming darkness while turning away from a bright lamp labelled justice, contrasted with a child facing the light, stark watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.
verses.little_bible: Punishment is ready and waiting for mockers. Fools will receive what their foolishness deserves.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Mockers and fools will be punished. God has prepared justice for them.
verses.meaning: The chapter closes with the certainty of divine justice. Scorners — those who mock wisdom, God, and truth — have judgment already prepared for them. Fools who persist in their folly will face the consequences their choices have earned. God's justice is not passive or delayed indefinitely; it is ready. This is not vindictiveness but righteousness: a holy God cannot leave scorn and foolishness permanently unpunished.
verses.prayer: God, help me never mock what is good and true.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to know that God has prepared justice for mockers?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that God's justice is not optional or delayed forever — and that this should motivate not fear but sober, reverent, joyful obedience to God's ways?
verses.do_it_today: Ask God to help you take His word seriously today — not mockingly or lightly, but with real respect and obedience.
verses.illustration_prompt: A gavel resting on a strong foundation, scales of justice balanced and certain, a child watching reverently in awe of God's righteous order, warm authoritative watercolour scene
